nora: quick heads-up — onboarding for nova-48k-q6 shows a tiny but consistent KV checksum flip after long prefill + streaming. repro below.

ben: paste the failing tail?

nora: minimal tail (prefill=33000 seed=13):
```
[2026-04-20T09:12:33Z] PREFILL: wrote 33000 tokens to KV(shard0)
[2026-04-20T09:12:36Z] KV_CHECK: window[32936..33000] expected=0x9f3c got=0x9f38
[2026-04-20T09:12:36Z] GENERATION: divergence at token_idx=33102
[2026-04-20T09:12:36Z] MODEL: max_pos=49152 prefill=33000 inflight=102 pos_mode=auto
```

kai: interesting — delta is small, like a few low bits. any phase dumps between fp16 and q6?

nora: ran `tools/phase_diff.py --model nova-48k-fp16 --quant q6 --start 32000 --end 33500` — saw a repeating micro-kink every ~1024 positions starting ~32k that flips a 16-bit window hash occasionally.

sylvia: could be LUT stride+packing. try `--force-angle=f16` and `--kv-flush-on-prefill=true`

bench-bot: summary run a1c4: model=nova-48k-q6 prefill=33000 throughput=8.9 toks/s kv_flip=1.2% reproducible=4/4 link: https://bench/rep/a1c4

nora: forcing f16-angle cleared 3/3. gating idea: onboarding harness set force-angle=f16 for q6 when prefill>30k. i'll open GH issue with diffs + hex-dump.

ben: i'll add a small unit test to assert monotonicity of quantized angles in 512-step windows. thanks — bringing kernel team in. :thumbsup:
